blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Diffusion and flow models generate a sample over iterative steps, each a full pass through a large network, and that pass dominates generation cost. Training-free caching accelerates them by reusing activations from recent evaluations instead of recomputing them. Dynamic caching methods decide when to refresh by accumulating a cheap probe of the network input into a staleness signal and spending a fresh evaluation once it crosses a threshold. They perform hard caching: the signal is a binary switch between refresh and reuse, and every step, fresh or cached, advances by the prescribed step size. We observe that the signal carries much more than this switch. How far it sits below the threshold, its headroom, predicts the error induced by reuse. We propose SoftCache, which performs soft caching: instead of a binary switch, the headroom sets how far each cached step goes. Where the headroom is large, the sampler jumps past several scheduled nodes, and as a refresh nears, its steps shrink back toward the original step. These adaptive jumps may land between the scheduled nodes, taking the sampler off its fixed grid. SoftCache requires no training and adds no per-backbone settings: on FLUX for images and on HunyuanVideo and Wan2.1 for video, at speedups from $3.5\times$ to $6.9\times$, it is ahead of every baseline on all four fidelity metrics.
blocks.zh: 分流和流出模型在迭代步骤上生成一个样本,每一个都通过一个大型网络,而通过这个模式则支配了生成成本. 无训练的缓存通过重新使用最近评价的活化物而不是重算来加速它们。 动态缓存方法通过将网络输入的廉价探测器积累到停滞信号中,然后在超过阈值后花费新的评价,决定何时刷新. 它们执行硬缓冲:信号是介于刷新和再利用之间的二进制开关,每个步骤,新鲜或缓冲,按规定的步长前进. 我们发现信号比这个开关要多得多 它坐落到阈值以下多远,它的头室,预测了再利用引起的出错. 我们提出SoftCache,它执行软缓存: 而不是二进制开关, 头室设定每个缓存步骤的去向。 在主室很大的地方,采样器会跳过几个预定的节点,而作为一个新鲜的接近点,它的台阶会缩回原来的台阶. 这些适应性跳跃可能降落在预定的节点之间,使采样器脱离了固定的网格. blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Diffusion and flow models set the state of the art in image
and video synthesis ( Black Forest Labs, 2024 ; Kong et al., 2024 ; Wan et al., 2025 ; Esser et al., 2024 ) .
These models are slow at inference: producing a single output requires
tens of full network evaluations, each a pass through the same large transformer.
Yet the latent changes only slightly between steps, so successive
passes largely recompute what the previous one already produced.
This redundancy is the resource that acceleration methods draw on, and they
differ in what they are willing to give up to reach it.
In practice, this is done using
distillation ( Song et al., 2023 ; Salimans & Ho, 2022 ) , fewer-step
solvers ( Song et al., 2021a ; Lu et al., 2022 ; Zhao et al., 2023 ) , or cheaper
attention ( Yuan et al., 2024 ; Xi et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025b ; Zhang et al., 2025a ) ,
each with its own cost in training, calibration, or fidelity.

A different lever is to reuse the model’s own output, i.e., caching ,
instead of solving faster or attending more cheaply.
Successive steps can then share computation directly rather than recompute
it.
Every cache must still decide when to refresh, and many settle this before
sampling begins, with a refresh pattern that is fixed in advance and shared by every
prompt ( Ma et al., 2024 ; Selvaraju et al., 2024 ; Liu et al., 2025b ; Cui et al., 2026 ; Aliev et al., 2026 ) . Dynamic caches instead make refresh timing their central question and
decide it during sampling: a cheap probe of the network predicts how much its
output is about to change, and this signal decides, per prompt, when the
cached computation has gone stale ( Liu et al., 2025a ; Chung et al., 2026 ) .

We observe that this ignored distance is informative. Below the threshold,
the signal closely tracks the reuse error, the gap between the cached
computation and a fresh one at the current node. The
distance from the threshold, which we call the headroom , measures
how safely the cache can be trusted, and we use it to set the step size
instead of only the refresh decision: this is soft caching .
When the headroom is large, the cache is still reliable, so the sampler takes
a long step that skips several scheduled nodes and can land between them
( Fig. 1 ). When the headroom is small, refresh is near, so the step
shrinks back toward the scheduled one. We call this method SoftCache: the headroom sets the step continuously rather
than picking how many nodes to skip, and every node a step passes over is
one the sampler no longer visits.

blocks.en:
Set against both kinds of cache, this is a different form of adaptivity. A
fixed schedule refreshes at the same nodes for every prompt. A dynamic
cache refreshes at nodes that vary with the prompt, but at scheduled nodes
all the same. Here the steps vary with the prompt too, and they also land
where no node was scheduled. This freedom translates into fidelity: on
FLUX, HunyuanVideo and Wan2.1, against caches of both kinds at comparable
speed, SoftCache reproduces the uncached model most faithfully on every
metric at every operating point we test.
Adaptivity, then, does not stop at deciding when to refresh. It also
decides where the sampler goes next.

blocks.en:
Our main contributions are:
(1) We identify that the refresh signal of a dynamic cache carries more than a
binary decision: its headroom below the threshold tracks the reuse error, so it
measures how far the cached computation can still be trusted.
(2) We propose SoftCache, which reads the headroom as a step size: cached steps
jump off the scheduler’s grid in proportion to it, the tail is re-spaced so
that every node passed is dropped from the trajectory, and the cached residual is
extrapolated linearly to the landing, at no extra network cost.
(3) On image and video backbones, SoftCache adds no per-backbone settings
and is ahead of every cache we compare on all four fidelity metrics in
every speed band from 3.5 × 3.5\times to 6.9 × 6.9\times .

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Diffusion sampling acceleration
blocks.zh: 2.1 传播取样加速

blocks.en:
Methods that cut sampling cost differ in what they modify. Some change the network or a
single evaluation of it: distillation trains a student that needs fewer
steps ( Song et al., 2023 ; Salimans & Ho, 2022 ; Luo et al., 2023 ) , while sparse
attention ( Yuan et al., 2024 ; Xi et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025b ; Zhang et al., 2025a ) and token
reduction ( Bolya et al., 2023 ) make each step cheaper. Others change the grid: higher-order
solvers reach a given quality in fewer steps ( Song et al., 2021a ; Lu et al., 2022 ; Zhao et al., 2023 ) ,
and schedule design places the steps where they matter
most ( Karras et al., 2022 ; Esser et al., 2024 ; Sabour et al., 2024 ) .
We work in a third family, caching, which changes neither the network nor an evaluation
of it: it exploits the redundancy between neighboring states along the trajectory and
reuses computation from earlier steps, without training.

blocks.en: 2.2 Feature caching
blocks.zh: 2.2 地物缓存

blocks.en:
Caching methods differ in what they store and when they refresh it. The stored
quantity ranges from intermediate activations of U-Net or transformer
blocks ( Ma et al., 2024 ; Selvaraju et al., 2024 ; Liu et al., 2025b ) to the residual
of a span of blocks or of the entire
stack ( Chen et al., 2024 ; Liu et al., 2025a ; Chung et al., 2026 ) , and it may be
refreshed for only a subset of tokens ( Zou et al., 2025 ; Zou et al., 2024 ; Zheng et al., 2025b ) .
Fixed schedules refresh periodically ( Ma et al., 2024 ; Selvaraju et al., 2024 ; Liu et al., 2025b ) or at steps chosen offline, by thresholding a reuse error calibrated on a few
samples ( Ma et al., 2025 ; Peng et al., 2026 ) or by
optimizing for a fixed budget of full evaluations ( Cui et al., 2026 ; Aliev et al., 2026 ) .
Online rules refresh once an accumulated cheap proxy of the output change crosses a
threshold ( Liu et al., 2025a ; Chung et al., 2026 ; Nam et al., 2026 ; Bu et al., 2025 ) .
Such rules therefore refreshe at different nodes for different prompts,
whereas a fixed schedule applies one refresh pattern to all of them.
Either way, each node, or token, makes one binary choice between a full evaluation
and reuse. SoftCache refreshes on the same spectral signal ( Chung et al., 2026 ) ,
but also reads its headroom below the threshold to make reuse soft rather than binary.

blocks.en: 2.3 Predictive caching
blocks.zh: 2.3 预测性缓存

blocks.en:
Between refreshes, most caches hold the stored quantity
fixed ( Ma et al., 2024 ; Selvaraju et al., 2024 ; Liu et al., 2025a ; Chung et al., 2026 ) ,
so the reuse error grows with the time since the last refresh. Predictive caches
extrapolate from recent history instead. Some forecast what the network returns,
the output of the block stack ( Cui et al., 2026 ) ,
its increment over the input ( Bu et al., 2025 ) , or the velocity itself ( Wang et al., 2026 ) .
Others forecast the increment each attention and MLP
branch adds to its input, which the current node applies to its own activations,
with Taylor ( Liu et al., 2025b ) or Hermite ( Feng et al., 2026 ) coefficients built from several stored past values.
Multistep formulas ( Yu et al., 2025 ; Zheng et al., 2025a ) and a check on the
prediction ( Liu et al., 2025c ) extend how far it can be carried. All of them
predict only at the nodes of the sampler’s schedule, so the schedule itself is
untouched. We extrapolate an increment as well, a single one for the entire stack,
along the straight line through the two most recent fresh evaluations. Written in
the flow time, that line is defined between nodes, which is what lets the sampler
leave the schedule rather than only skip evaluations along it.

blocks.en: 2.4 Adaptive step size control
blocks.zh: 2.4 适应步骤大小控制

blocks.en:
Adaptive ODE solvers set each step at runtime from an estimate of the local error,
obtained by comparing two solutions of different order ( Dormand & Prince, 1980 ) ,
and the same control has been applied to diffusion sampling in both its
SDE ( Jolicoeur-Martineau et al., 2021 ) and ODE ( Lu et al., 2022 ) forms.
The estimate costs several network evaluations per step, which is the computation a
cache exists to avoid. SoftCache takes its step size from the refresh signal the cache
already computes, so the schedule adapts at no evaluations beyond those the cache spends
anyway.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We presented SoftCache, a training-free method that turns hard caching into
soft caching. A dynamic cache already measures how stale its cached
computation has become, but spends the measurement on a binary choice between
refresh and reuse. SoftCache reads the headroom below the threshold as how far
the cache can still be trusted and lets it set the step size: cached steps
jump past scheduled nodes while the cache is reliable and shrink back to the
scheduled step as a refresh nears, the tail is re-spaced so that every node
passed is dropped from the trajectory, and the cached residual is extrapolated to each
off-grid landing at no extra network cost.
On FLUX, HunyuanVideo and Wan2.1, at wall-clock speedups from 3.5 × 3.5\times to 6.9 × 6.9\times , SoftCache stays closest to the uncached sample on all
four fidelity metrics, with no per-model calibration.
Adaptivity in caching, then, does not stop at deciding when to refresh.

blocks.en: D.1 What the fidelity metrics measure
blocks.zh: D.1 联合国 忠诚度量衡是什么

blocks.en:
PSNR is a per-pixel error, so it rewards an output that drifts toward a smooth conditional mean
and penalises one that keeps sharp detail slightly out of place. At high speedups a blurred output
can therefore outscore a sharper one that looks closer to the reference. Fig. D.1.1 shows such a case. On one HunyuanVideo clip at a similar speedup,
SeaCache leads SoftCache by 3.19 3.19 dB in PSNR, yet its foliage is visibly blurred (inset), and SSIM,
LPIPS and DreamSim all favour SoftCache. We therefore report PSNR in every table but never decide on
it alone, and we back the ablation choices with blind visual comparisons ( Sec. C.3 ).
blocks.zh:
PSNR 是一个每像素错误,所以它奖励一个向平滑条件平均值漂移的输出
并惩罚一个 保持尖锐的细节略离位置。 在高速运行时输出模糊
因此,可以比更尖锐的更接近参考。 图D.1.1显示了这种情况。 在Hunyuan Video的一段类似速度的片段上,
SeaCache在PSNR中以3.19 3.19 dB引导SoftCache,然而它的叶片明显模糊(inset),而SSIM,
LPIPS和DreamSim都倾向于软卡切. 因此,我们在每个表格中报告PSNR,但从未决定
我们用盲目的视觉对比来回击禁欲选择(C.
